clue.text: Not having succeeded at the front, cut and run

indicators.note: not having tells you the word for cut goes without the letter that succeeded gives
at the front says the missing letter is the first one of the word for cut

parts.note: a cut is a share of the takings
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in genealogies and lists of monarchs

explanation.surface: A soldier who got nowhere on the front line gives up and flees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut and run' is a fixed phrase, but it splits: 'cut' is a share of the proceeds, which loses its first letter ('Not having ... at the front'), and 'run' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: to dash off at great speed, as the animal does.

clue.text: Cut the harsh words: cricketer bagging 500 is opener for England

indicators.note: bagging means catching and holding, so the cricketer takes the numeral inside

parts.note: a bowler is the cricketer who delivers the ball to the batsman
D is the Roman numeral for 500

indicators.note: the opener for a word is its first letter, as an opening batsman goes in first

explanation.surface: After the swearing is edited out, the report says a cricketer with 500 runs goes in first for England.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket runs right through: 'bagging' puts D inside the cricketer, and 'opener for' is not an opening batsman but the first letter of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb: to expurgate a text by removing anything offensive, after Thomas Bowdler's sanitised Shakespeare.

clue.text: It doesn't take much to make one mad

definitions.text: It doesn't take much to make one mad

parts.words: It doesn't take much to make one mad
parts.note: not someone quick to anger: a person whose madness needs only a single subject, so very little is required

explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: a person obsessed with a single idea needs just that lone subject to be driven crazy.

clue.text: Encourage burst of speed, being short of finish

indicators.note: being short of its finish means the word for a burst of speed lacks its last letter

parts.note: a spurt is a sudden burst of speed

explanation.surface: Cheer on a sprinter whose late dash fades just before the line.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: to urge someone on, as a rider urges a horse with the heel.

clue.text: Question about curtailment of holiday expected to have problems?

indicators.note: about means the questioning word goes around the shortened holiday

parts.note: to question someone is to ask them

indicators.note: curtailment is cutting the tail off, so the holiday word loses its last letter

parts.note: a trip is a holiday or journey

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether cutting a holiday short is likely to cause trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym phrase: someone in danger is likely to meet trouble; the question mark allows the loose wording.

clue.text: Computer storage needing energy after battery failed

indicators.note: after says the letter for energy follows the rearranged word
something that has failed is broken, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A computer's disk needs a new power source once its battery has died.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a unit of digital capacity, a trillion bytes, by which disk size is measured.

clue.text: Look happy, finishing chore early

indicators.note: finishing, read with early, says the chore word stops before its last letter
early completes finishing: the word ends one letter sooner than it should

parts.note: a grind is a tedious, wearying chore

explanation.surface: Someone beams because the housework was done ahead of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: to smile broadly is to show pleasure on your face.

clue.text: Left air force initially in debt, perhaps, habitual convict

indicators.note: in puts the single letter from force inside the run made by the two pieces that follow

parts.note: in the red means in debt, so debt, perhaps, is those last two words
a lag is slang for a habitual convict, as in 'old lag'

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A man who quit the air force starts civilian life owing money, possibly a repeat offender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left air force' reads as one phrase but splits after 'air': the Left's air is the socialist anthem sung by Britain's Labour Party. 'in' puts F ('initially' from force) inside THE RED plus LAG.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: the anthem (air) of socialists and of Britain's Labour movement, the political Left.

clue.text: It pins down what law enforcement agencies feel?

definitions.text: It pins down what law enforcement agencies feel?

parts.words: It pins down what law enforcement agencies feel?
parts.note: in British slang the police 'feel your collar' when they arrest you; taken literally, 'it' is the small fastener that holds that part of a shirt in place

explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: a small fastener securing a shirt's detachable neckband, the very thing police proverbially grab when arresting someone.

clue.text: Crowd's heading off in a hurry

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter of the crowd word is removed

parts.note: a crush is a dense, packed crowd of people

explanation.surface: The crowd is leaving quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' is not the crowd leaving: it removes the first letter of CRUSH.
explanation.definitionFit: Noun synonym: haste, as when you are pressed for time.

clue.text: Dodge that is retained in heads of some exciting players

indicators.note: retained in means the Latin phrase is kept inside the three initial letters
heads of takes the first letter of each of the three words after it

parts.note: id est is the Latin for 'that is', usually shortened to i.e.

explanation.surface: Some thrilling rugby players keep a clever swerve stored in their heads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that is' is not the usual IE but the full Latin ID EST, 'retained in' S, E, P, the first letters ('heads of') of some exciting players.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: to evade something by moving quickly aside.

clue.text: Not happy about a grand display of humbug

indicators.note: about means the word for not happy goes around the two letters

parts.note: blue means sad or downcast
G is short for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: Someone is displeased by a showy piece of hypocrisy.
explanation.definitionFit: Noun borrowed from French: pretentious nonsense or a hoax, which is what humbug amounts to.

clue.text: Sound of crowd running on and rioting in opening stages

indicators.note: the opening stage of each of the four words before it is its first letter

explanation.surface: The noise of a mob charging forward as a riot begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the loud collective noise that a stadium of spectators makes.

clue.text: Like many a monastery, so derelict after Reformation

indicators.note: re-formation is forming again, so the two words before it are given a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Many monasteries were left in ruins after the Reformation.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital R points at Henry VIII closing England's monasteries, a true picture, but 'after Reformation' only means re-formed: the letters of 'so derelict' in a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective: enclosed, or having covered walkways round a quadrangle, as religious houses typically are.

clue.text: Political group, some investing in recycled energy

indicators.note: investing in means the word for some is put inside the rearranged word
recycled things are reprocessed, so the letters of the word after it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
part of something is some of it

explanation.surface: A political group with members putting their money into renewable power.
explanation.walkthrough: Beyond the mechanics, the whole clue paints the answer: a movement keen on putting money into renewable power.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a real organisation that fights elections on environmental issues.

clue.text: Carry the fifth child?

parts.note: a tot is a small child
E is the fifth letter of the alphabet: label the children A, B, C and so on, and the fifth one carries this letter

explanation.surface: A parent holding their fifth baby.
explanation.walkthrough: Whimsical: if a family's children were lettered in order, the fifth would be the child marked with the fifth letter. The question mark admits the liberty.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: to lug or haul something by hand.

clue.text: Excellent soldiers, including Bill, one affected by experience

indicators.note: including means the run made by excellent and soldiers takes the bill word inside it

parts.note: A1, written AI, means first-rate
a bill is a poster stuck on a wall, as in 'post no bills'
OR is the military abbreviation for other ranks, the ordinary soldiers
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Bill is one of a fine body of troops, a man marked by what he has been through.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital letter makes Bill a comrade in the ranks; it is really a notice pasted on a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin phrase for reasoning from observed facts back to causes, so knowledge of this kind depends on what has been lived through.

clue.text: I'm not alone, forgetting one name when drunk, like this?

indicators.note: a drunk is unsteady and muddled, so the letters left are jumbled into a new order
forgetting means a letter is left out of the phrase before it

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
N abbreviates name, and only one of the phrase's two Ns is dropped

explanation.surface: A tipsy person insists they have company but cannot recall somebody's name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forgetting' drops one N from IM NOT ALONE and 'when drunk' rearranges the remaining nine letters. 'this' points back at the drunken state the clue has just described.
explanation.definitionFit: Reference back: 'tired and emotional' is a British euphemism for tipsy, coined by the magazine Private Eye.

clue.text: Support framework beset by risk

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded, so the framework sits inside the risk word

parts.note: a bet is a risk, a gamble
a rack is a framework for holding things

explanation.surface: The scaffolding holding a building up is surrounded by danger.
explanation.definitionFit: Noun synonym: a projecting piece fixed to a wall to hold up a shelf.

clue.text: No peeping allowed during this journey?

definitions.text: No peeping allowed during this journey?

parts.words: No peeping allowed during this journey?
parts.note: peeping is not sneaky looking but the shrill sound a guard or referee blows; the trip's name, taken literally, says such blowing must cease

explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: a rapid trip of many brief halts, like a campaigning politician's, whose name read literally bans shrill blasts.

clue.text: University nuclear research centre in the Francophone Swiss city

indicators.note: in puts the university letter and the research centre inside the French article

parts.note: le is the word 'the' as a French speaker says it
CERN is the European nuclear research organisation near Geneva

explanation.surface: A university's atomic laboratory is found in the French-speaking Swiss town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Francophone' belongs with 'the', giving LE, not with the city: the place itself is German-speaking, which is the trap.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a lakeside town in central Switzerland, known for its wooden Chapel Bridge.

clue.text: Suggest top may be taken off without difficulty

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter, which is removed from the word that follows

parts.note: simply means easily, without difficulty

explanation.surface: A hint that a garment could be slipped off easily.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: to hint at something without stating it outright.

clue.text: Curious passion arising in middle of week

indicators.note: in puts the upturned passion word between the two letters taken from week
middle of takes the two central letters of the word that follows
arising means rising, so in a down clue the passion word is read upwards

parts.note: ire is anger, a strong passion

explanation.surface: A strange longing stirs on a Wednesday.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym in the sense of strange or uncanny, an older meaning than inquisitive.

clue.text: Lantern's cut out for offering some light

indicators.note: out means out of order, so the letters of the two words before it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lantern has had shapes pierced in it so that it gives off a glow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut out' reads as one verb, but 'cut' is fodder with LANTERNS and 'out' alone tells you to rearrange them.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective: letting a diffuse glow pass through without giving a clear view.

clue.text: Strong ending to hymn, perhaps — time to indicate heaven?

parts.note: firm means strong and solid
amen is the word sung to close a hymn or prayer

explanation.surface: A rousing last verse of the hymn is the moment to point the congregation's thoughts skyward.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the vault of the sky, a poetic and biblical word for the heavens.

clue.text: Set local limit on speed, endlessly rising speed

parts.note: rate is speed, as in rate of progress

indicators.note: rising means reading upwards in a down clue, so the shortened word is turned round
endlessly means the second speed word loses its last letter

parts.note: pace is another word for speed

explanation.surface: A council imposes a speed restriction while the traffic just keeps getting faster.
explanation.walkthrough: Rates were Britain's local property tax, and the government could limit what a council charged. 'endlessly' trims PACE to PAC and 'rising' turns it into CAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb: in Britain, to restrict the property tax a council may levy, hence 'local'.

clue.text: Abandon public transport, say, with no place for a source of music?

parts.note: to debus is to get off a bus

indicators.note: with no place for means the letter named next has no room in the word before it

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Give up on the buses, for instance, when there is no room aboard for a busker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like the usual 'for example' but supplies letters: 'with no place for' removes its A, leaving SY.
explanation.definitionFit: Example by description: the French composer of Clair de Lune, a person from whom tunes flow.

clue.text: Time of growth, though not new, little growth

indicators.note: though not says the season is without the letter that new gives

parts.note: spring is the season when plants start to grow
N abbreviates new, as on maps and in NT

explanation.surface: A growing season, hardly a recent one, produced only a small shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: Noun: a small shoot or twig, a tiny piece of a plant.

clue.text: Duke associated with libertine, an Elizabethan knight

indicators.note: associated with means the duke's letter is joined to the libertine word

parts.note: a rake is a dissolute man, a libertine

explanation.surface: A duke keeps company with a dissolute fellow who was knighted by Elizabeth I.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Sir Francis, the sea captain who sailed round the world, was knighted by Elizabeth I in 1581.
